title: Security Fundamentals
description: Master core security principles, threat detection, and tactical defense in bite-sized missions.

units.title: The CIA Triad & Core Defense
units.guidebook: The CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability) is the universal bedrock of information security. Confidentiality ensures data is accessible only to authorized entities through encryption, access control lists (ACLs), and data classification. Integrity guarantees information remains accurate and untampered with via cryptographic hashing and digital signatures. Availability ensures critical systems, networks, and databases are operational and reachable when needed through redundancy, backups, and load balancing.

exercises.title: Confidentiality in Action
exercises.content: Confidentiality prevents unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data. It relies on encryption, strong authentication, and principle of least privilege.
exercises.keyTakeaway: If someone doesn't need to see the data to do their job, they shouldn't have access.

exercises.prompt: Which principle of the CIA Triad focuses on keeping sensitive records secret from unauthorized parties?
exercises.explanation: Confidentiality protects secrets, passwords, and sensitive information from exposure.

exercises.prompt: A padlock icon (HTTPS) in the browser URL bar guarantees a website is safe and not operated by scammers.
exercises.explanation: HTTPS only encrypts the connection. Malicious attackers frequently obtain free SSL certificates for phishing sites.

exercises.prompt: Complete the security concept:
exercises.sentence: A ___ provides an encrypted tunnel that shields public Wi-Fi communications from snooping.
exercises.explanation: A Virtual Private Network (VPN) creates an encrypted tunnel across untrusted networks.

exercises.prompt: Match each security concept with its definition:
pairs: Ensuring systems are accessible when required
Inability to deny the authenticity of a signed action
exercises.explanation: These core concepts establish the security posture for all modern enterprise networks.

exercises.prompt: Select all effective safeguards that protect data confidentiality:
options: Broadcasting passwords on open team channels
Disabling screen locks on work laptops
exercises.explanation: Encryption, RBAC, and MFA restrict access to authorized individuals.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the standard NIST incident response phases in correct order:
exercises.explanation: NIST SP 800-61 starts with Preparation and ends with Post-Incident Lessons Learned.

exercises.prompt: What security principle states users should only have the minimum permissions needed to do their work?
exercises.explanation: Least privilege limits blast radius if an account is compromised.

exercises.title: Data Integrity & Hashes
exercises.content: Cryptographic hash functions (like SHA-256) generate a fixed-size fingerprint for any file. If even a single byte changes, the hash changes completely (the avalanche effect).
exercises.keyTakeaway: Cryptographic hashes verify that files have not been modified or corrupted.

exercises.prompt: Inspect this email header. Tap the suspicious sender address indicator:

threatData.subject: Account Alert: Unrecognized Device Logged In
threatData.body: We detected an unauthorized sign-in. Verify your account now or it will be locked.

exercises.explanation: The domain 'paypa1-security-verification.com' substitutes the letter 'l' with the digit '1' (typosquatting).

exercises.prompt: Construct the command to compute the SHA-256 hash of 'financial_report.pdf':
exercises.explanation: sha256sum outputs the 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 checksum of the target file.

exercises.context: A coworker sends you an executable file called 'QuarterlyBonus.exe' over chat, asking you to run it right away to claim your company bonus.
exercises.prompt: What is the safest tactical response?
options: Run the file immediately before the bonus expires
Scan the file on an external untrusted website and run it if clean
Do not run the file, contact your coworker through a different channel to verify, and notify security
Forward it to other team members to test if it works for them
exercises.explanation: Out-of-band verification and reporting prevents executing malware from a compromised coworker account.

exercises.prompt: Which cryptographic property guarantees that a digital signature cannot be easily forged or denied?
exercises.explanation: Non-repudiation provides irrefutable proof of the origin and integrity of a digital transaction.

exercises.prompt: A cryptographic hash function can be mathematically reversed to recover the original password.
exercises.explanation: Cryptographic hashes are one-way mathematical functions; you cannot reverse-engineer the input from the hash.

exercises.prompt: Complete the statement:
exercises.sentence: A digital signature uses asymmetric cryptography with a sender's ___ key to sign and the public key to verify.
exercises.explanation: The private key signs the data and only the matching public key can verify the signature.

exercises.prompt: Match the hashing algorithm to its security standing:
pairs: Slow, salted hash recommended for passwords
exercises.explanation: Always use modern algorithms like SHA-256 for integrity and Argon2/Bcrypt for passwords.

exercises.prompt: Which attack specifically aims to exhaust computing resources and render an online service unavailable?
exercises.explanation: DoS and DDoS attacks flood network pipes or CPU resources to take servers offline.

exercises.prompt: Select all key technologies used to guarantee high system availability:
exercises.explanation: Redundancy, load balancing, and failover eliminate single points of failure.

exercises.prompt: Order the steps of a structured disaster recovery procedure:
steps: Declare disaster and trigger emergency communication
Failover traffic to secondary data center
Verify system integrity and conduct root-cause review
exercises.explanation: A systematic disaster plan minimizes business downtime and avoids secondary data loss.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the curl command to inspect HTTP response headers and check server status:
exercises.explanation: The `-I` (or `--head`) flag fetches the HTTP header without downloading the body.

exercises.prompt: Spot the threat indicator in this suspicious text message (Smishing):

threatData.subject: USPS Package Delivery Delayed
threatData.body: USPS: Your parcel has an incorrect zip code. Update details within 24h at: https://usps-parcel-redirection-fee.info/pay

exercises.explanation: The domain 'usps-parcel-redirection-fee.info' is an untrusted scam URL mimicking the Postal Service.

exercises.context: A Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack strikes your e-commerce gateway on Black Friday, overwhelming the ingress routers.
exercises.prompt: What is the most effective immediate countermeasure?
options: Reboot the production web servers every 15 minutes
Route incoming traffic through a cloud DDoS mitigation and scrubbing provider
Disable all TLS certificates to reduce CPU load
Turn off the firewall to let traffic pass freely
exercises.explanation: Cloud scrubbing centers filter out malicious bot traffic while passing legitimate customer requests.

exercises.prompt: Ransomware attacks only threaten confidentiality, leaving system availability unaffected.
exercises.explanation: Ransomware severely damages availability by encrypting operational data and taking down core systems.

exercises.prompt: Complete the concept:
exercises.sentence: The maximum tolerable duration of downtime during an outage is defined in the SLA as the Recovery ___ Objective (RTO).
exercises.explanation: Recovery Time Objective (RTO) dictates how fast systems must be restored after disruption.

units.title: Threat Landscape & Active Defense
units.guidebook: Modern threat actors deploy sophisticated social engineering, malware, and automated reconnaissance against networks. Understanding offensive tradecraft enables blue teamers to implement proactive defenses. We examine phishing anatomy, malware categories, credential harvesting, defense-in-depth architecture, and essential command-line reconnaissance tools like Nmap.

exercises.title: The Art of Social Engineering
exercises.content: Social engineering exploits human psychology—urgency, authority, fear, and curiosity—rather than software bugs. Phishing accounts for over 80% of reported security incidents.
exercises.keyTakeaway: Always pause and question any communication demanding urgent action or financial transfers.

exercises.prompt: What type of phishing specifically targets high-profile executives or board members?
exercises.explanation: Whaling is spear-phishing directed specifically at executive leadership (the 'big fish').

exercises.prompt: Inspect this fake Microsoft 365 login link. Tap the deceptive indicator:

threatData.subject: Action Required: Re-authenticate your corporate email
threatData.body: Your session has expired. Log in here to retain access: http://login.microsoftonline.com.attacker-controlled-proxy.ru/signin

exercises.explanation: The domain ends in '.attacker-controlled-proxy.ru' despite prepending 'login.microsoftonline.com' as subdomains.

exercises.prompt: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) that uses SMS text codes is immune to SIM-swapping attacks.
exercises.explanation: SMS-based MFA is vulnerable to SIM-swap fraud and interception. Hardware keys (FIDO2) or authenticator apps are much more secure.

exercises.context: An urgent phone caller claims to be your company's CEO calling from an airport, demanding you immediately wire $50,000 to a new vendor account before the flight departs.
exercises.prompt: What attack vector does this represent?
options: Business Email Compromise / CEO Vishing Fraud
exercises.explanation: CEO fraud uses authority and artificial urgency over phone (vishing) or email to bypass financial controls.

exercises.prompt: Match the social engineering vector to its medium:
pairs: Leaving infected physical USB drives in public areas
exercises.explanation: Recognizing varied channels helps users detect social engineering attacks.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the blank:
exercises.sentence: A physical security attack where an unauthorized person follows an employee through a secure badge door is called ___.
exercises.explanation: Tailgating (or piggybacking) breaches perimeter defenses by exploiting social courtesy.

exercises.prompt: Construct the WHOIS command to inspect the domain registration and owner details of 'malicious-domain.com':
exercises.explanation: whois queries registry databases for domain registrar, creation date, and contact details.

exercises.prompt: Order the typical stages of the Cyber Kill Chain (Lockheed Martin framework):
steps: Command & Control (C2) and Actions on Objectives
exercises.explanation: Understanding the attack kill chain allows defenders to disrupt the intrusion at early stages.

exercises.prompt: Select all typical characteristics of Ransomware:
options: Encrypts user documents and system files
Demands cryptocurrency payment for decryption keys
Leaves a ransom note on the desktop
exercises.explanation: Ransomware holds user data hostage through encryption and cryptocurrency extortion.

exercises.prompt: What differentiates a Computer Worm from a standard Computer Virus?
options: A worm can self-replicate and spread across networks without human action
A worm only affects mobile smartphones
A worm requires the user to open an infected document
A worm cannot be detected by antivirus scanners
exercises.explanation: Worms propagate autonomously across network vulnerabilities without needing a host program or user trigger.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the Nmap command to scan top 100 ports with service version detection on 10.0.0.1:
exercises.explanation: The `-F` flag runs a fast scan of top 100 ports, and `-sV` probes for service/version info.

exercises.prompt: Spot the suspicious base64 obfuscated payload in this PowerShell execution snippet:
exercises.explanation: The `-Enc` flag decodes and executes an obfuscated base64 payload in memory.

exercises.prompt: Complete the security term:
exercises.sentence: A software vulnerability unknown to the software vendor with no patch yet available is called a ___-day vulnerability.
exercises.explanation: Zero-day vulnerabilities represent severe risks because no vendor remediation exists yet.

exercises.context: Your EDR (Endpoint Detection and Response) console reports an employee laptop beaconing every 60 seconds to a known Cobalt Strike C2 IP address.
exercises.prompt: What is the very first containment action you should take?
options: Reboot the machine to see if the connection stops
Isolate the infected host from the network immediately
Delete the operating system files immediately
Wait 48 hours to collect more data before intervening
exercises.explanation: Network isolation stops lateral movement and active data exfiltration while preserving memory forensics.

exercises.prompt: Running as an Administrator or root user for everyday web browsing is a safe security practice.
exercises.explanation: Browser exploits running with administrator privileges grant attackers instant full machine control.

exercises.title: Defense-in-Depth Architecture
exercises.content: A fortified network utilizes tiered defensive perimeters: Next-Gen Firewalls at the perimeter, zero-trust network segmentation, endpoint protection on hosts, and centralized SIEM log monitoring.
exercises.keyTakeaway: Layered defenses ensure that a single bypassed lock does not yield total network takeover.

exercises.prompt: Match each network security tool to its primary function:
pairs: Network mapping and open port scanning
exercises.explanation: Security professionals leverage these tools for audits, monitoring, and forensic defense.

exercises.prompt: Order the steps of the TCP 3-way handshake:
exercises.explanation: The SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK handshake establishes a reliable TCP connection.

exercises.prompt: Construct the netstat command to show all active listening TCP ports with process IDs:
exercises.explanation: The `-tulnp` options display TCP/UDP listening sockets with numeric ports and process names.

exercises.prompt: Inspect this SQL query input field. Tap the classic SQL Injection (SQLi) attempt:

threatData.subject: SQLi Detected in Login Form
threatData.body: User input for username: admin' OR '1'='1' --

exercises.explanation: ' OR '1'='1' -- is the classic SQL injection string designed to force a true clause and bypass authentication.

exercises.context: An audit discovers that your internal database server is accessible directly over the public internet on default port 3306 with password authentication only.
exercises.prompt: What architectural change should be implemented immediately?
options: Restrict database access to internal private subnets or VPN only, behind a firewall
Increase the password length by 2 characters and leave it public
Change port 3306 to port 3307 and keep it exposed
Post a warning banner on the connection page
exercises.explanation: Databases should never be exposed to the public internet. Use private VPC subnets and VPN/bastion access.

exercises.prompt: Select all essential hardening steps for securing a new production Linux server:
options: Disable SSH root login and password authentication (use SSH keys)
Enable an active firewall (UFW/iptables) allowing only required ports
Leave all default vendor accounts with default passwords
Disable system logging to save hard drive space
exercises.explanation: SSH key authentication, firewalls, and timely patching form the baseline of Linux hardening.

exercises.prompt: Which network architecture model requires every user and device inside or outside the network to be authenticated and continuously validated?
exercises.explanation: The Zero Trust model follows the mantra: 'Never trust, always verify'.
